sara (PM): Quick sync — we need a short spec for hybrid sequential+parallel tool calling. customer asks: run some steps in parallel, but guarantee a rollback/compensate if a later step fails. what's a realistic MVP?

>dana (eng): MVP constraints: per-step timeouts, idempotency tokens, and a clear fallback path. full 2PC is hard across external integrations. recommend compensating actions instead of blocking commits.

>mike (eng-runtime): Agree. runtime can support grouping steps into parallel groups and then a final commit step. proposed API: an "execution_mode" and optional "compensate" block per step. example payload:```json
{
  "execution_mode": "hybrid",
  "idempotency_key": "txn_123",
  "steps": [
    { "name": "fetch_user", "type": "call", "timeout_ms": 2000 },
    { "name": "charge_card", "type": "call", "timeout_ms": 5000, "parallel_group": "billing" },
    { "name": "notify_teams", "type": "call", "parallel_group": "billing" },
    { "name": "finalize", "type": "call", "timeout_ms": 3000, "commit_policy": "compensate" }
  ]
}```

>raj (product): Quick question: how do we express "best-effort" rollback vs "must-succeed" commit? customers want clear SLAs.

>mike (eng-runtime): Add per-step "commit_policy": ["none","compensate","blocking"]. MVP supports "compensate" (fire compensator if later failure) and "none". "blocking" (wait for all downstream guarantees) is v2.

>olivia (sec): Security note: compensating actions may leak state; require explicit consent in policy for operations that mutate PII or billing. enforce KMS usage and audit logs for any rollback action.

>dana (eng): Retry budget: runtime will allocate a per-invocation retry budget (e.g., 3 total retries across all steps) and a group-level backoff to avoid thundering when parallel group fails. also we should expose a "retry_budget" and "group_backoff_ms" fields in API.

>sara (PM): Launch criteria proposal: 1) API shape stable for hybrid mode + idempotency, 2) runtime supports parallel groups + compensators, 3) docs + quickstart + 3 customer trials, 4) security signoff on compensators. thumbs? :thumbsup: needs consensus on "blocking" vs "compensate" default.

>raj (product): My take: default to "compensate" (safer) and surface a flag to opt into stronger semantics later. customers who need strict serial guarantees can use a sequential-only mode or reserve Dedicated capacity for advanced blocking semantics.

>mike (eng-runtime): Implementation notes:
- scheduler marks parallel groups and executes them concurrently.
- when a downstream step fails with a non-retryable error, runtime enqueues compensators for upstream steps that declared "compensate".
- compensators run asynchronously by default, but API can request "wait_for_compensators": true.
- we must add observability: per-step traces, compensator status, and an overall execution status: ["succeeded","failed","compensating","compensated"].

>dana (eng): Edge cases: external idempotency false negatives. require idempotency_key and return a stable execution id. clients should be able to query execution state via GET /executions/{id}. include full step logs for audits.

>olivia (sec): Also require explicit TTL for compensator actions and an allowlist for endpoints that can be auto-compensated. otherwise we risk runaway rollbacks.

>ops-bot: NOTE: perf impact estimate — optimistic: parallel groups will increase tail tokens by ~8-15% due to KV cache warmups; batching unaffected. add as doc note.

>sara (PM): Next steps: dana/mike draft an API PR with examples + reconcile with security constraints. raj will draft launch criteria and customer comms. goal: RFC in 2 weeks. thanks everyone.
